_comment: MCP channel configuration (Phase 8). Read by policies/mcp/invocation.rego.
WHAT THIS DOCUMENT IS: the set of actions that may be reached over the MCP
transport at all. It is a RISK decision -- 'should this be remotely
invocable by an agent holding an OAuth token?' -- and risk decisions belong
in configuration a risk owner changes, not in Python a developer changes.
WHAT THIS DOCUMENT IS NOT: an authorization grant. An action on this list is
merely CARRIABLE over MCP. Whether a particular agent may perform it is
decided by every ordinary rule in the set -- credential validity, capability,
resource scope, purpose scope, sensitive-action escalation, amount bands,
approvals and mandates -- exactly as it would be on any other channel.
Adding an action here can never widen what an agent may do; it can only stop
narrowing it.
WHY `execute_payment` IS ABSENT, and this is the substantive risk decision
in this file. A payment instruction is already carried by the Phase 7 A2A
channel, where it arrives inside an envelope signed by the instructing
agent's own Ed25519 key, bound to a receiver, non-replayable, and reconciled
against the server's figure four separate times. An MCP tools/call carries a
bearer token and nothing else: there is no signed instruction, so there is
no artifact to show a human during approval and nothing to non-repudiate
with afterwards. Exposing payments over a bearer-authenticated transport
would be a strictly weaker path to the same action, and the weaker path is
the one an attacker takes.
WHY `approve_loan` IS PRESENT despite being sensitive. It is reachable, but
reaching it is not the same as doing it: security/sensitive.rego escalates
it to a human and loan/amount.rego decides how many, so an MCP client can
at most OPEN an approval request. Dual control is unaffected by the channel
the request arrived on, which is the property Phase 8's tests assert.
FAILS CLOSED: mcp/invocation.rego denies with MCP_POLICY_UNCONFIGURED when
this document is not loaded. An absent list is never 'everything'.
